question: What is the API reading in Shah Alam right now?
name: Claude
answer:
Shah Alam's API is in the **unhealthy** range, roughly 165 to 180, based on the most recent reports I found for 16 Oct 2026. I can't pull the live APIMS feed, so these are news reports and not a real-time reading.

- **5pm:** Focus Malaysia, citing APIMS, put Shah Alam at **180**.
- **6pm:** Media Selangor, also citing APIMS, put it at **165**. That article's timestamp doesn't match its 6pm claim, so treat this figure with some caution.
- **Earlier in the day:** readings were about 168 to 171 (Bernama and Malay Mail).

If the 6pm figure is right, air quality improved slightly into the evening. Both figures fall in the 101–200 "unhealthy" band. The scale runs 0–50 good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy, 201–300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.

For the current hourly figure, check the official APIMS portal (apims.doe.gov.my) or semakapi.my. When the air is unhealthy, it's sensible to limit outdoor exertion and wear an N95 mask outdoors, especially if you have respiratory problems.

# Klang records Malaysia’s highest API reading; 34 areas face unhealthy air quality
A TOTAL of 34 locations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality readings as of 5pm today, with Klang, Selangor topping the list at an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 195.

Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed that Johor had the highest number of affected locations, with eight areas registering unhealthy readings.

Johan Setia recorded an API of 192, followed by Shah Alam at 180, Banting at 174, Petaling Jaya at 169 and Kuala Selangor at 161.



Negeri Sembilan had three affected areas, namely Nilai with an API of 191, Seremban at 181 and Port Dickson at 173.

Outside the peninsula, Kemaman in Terengganu registered 138, while Sandakan in Sabah recorded 125 and Samarahan in Sarawak stood at 117.

Separately, 34 locations recorded moderate air quality, while none registered good readings.

Under the API classification, readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, while readings between 51 and 100 are considered moderate.

Levels from 101 to 200 are classified as unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 indicate very unhealthy conditions. Any reading above 300 falls under the hazardous category.—Oct 16, 2026

SHAH ALAM, Oct 16 — Three Johor towns had Malaysia’s highest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at 6pm today: Pasir Gudang (199), Larkin (198), and Pengerang (181), all in the unhealthy category.

An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and anything above 300 is hazardous.
